import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

No, `.` and `;` don't work at the start of a bullet yet. I wrote a plan for the fix, it passed validation, and it's staged for your approval. No code has changed in either repo.

**What I tested with the current `bob` build** (using a throwaway vault with a `cash.md`):

| Draft (caret at end) | Result |
|---|---|
| `@cash^goog-exit@` + `- .` or `- ;` | `capture-rewrite` leaves it unchanged, so no `^`/`:` and no picker |
| `@cash:goog-exit@` + `- .` or `- ;` | Unchanged too |
| `@cash^goog-exit@` + `- ^` or `- :` | Opens the Move picker correctly |
| `@cash:goog-exit@` + `- ^` or `- :` | **Opens nothing**, an older bug |

**Two problems:**
1. **The alias was never allowed there.** The first plan only covered `.`/`;` right after `@route` and a whole-item `;`; your "route" choice left out the bullet positions.
2. **Under the `@foo:bar@` seal, even a real `^` or `:` doesn't open the Move picker.** Completion only recognizes the `@foo^bar@` seal. Everything else accepts both seals: `capture-parse` asks for the Move picker, `bob capture` performs the moves, and both repos' docs say it works under either seal. In Mac Capture today you get the "Pick a task to move" prompt with no picker behind it.

Mac Capture already sends every `.`/`;` keystroke to bob and lets bob decide. So the fix is mostly in bob-cli: make the Move picker accept both seals, then let the alias rule fire wherever that picker would open. The Mac side mainly needs tests built from real bob output, plus docs.

**One decision for you at approval: `choice_alias`** (default: on). Should `- ..` give the `- ^^` "choose several tasks" marker? If on, bob turns `- ^.` into `- ^^`. It also tells the open Move picker that `.` can stand in for its `^` key, which needs a small key-handling change in Mac Capture. If off, a second `.` just types into the picker's search filter.

The plan leaves out `.`/`;` typed at the end of a bullet (` .` / ` ;`), since you asked only about the start.

The plan also notes that `just lint` already fails on eight Clippy errors in files this work doesn't touch. One `just test` failure is tracked in `bob-cli-h5`; neither comes from this work.
